title: Joint transport of the completed quotient and Koszul presentations
statement: Let T be a scheme and d a Noetherian adic coefficient datum over A as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. There is an equivalence F from the actual completed-coefficient derived category to the derived category over the small-site constant completed ring. For every derived object K, F carries the actual total derived inverse limit of its strict quotient tower to constant quotient completion, carrying the actual constant/limit-adjunction unit followed by the specified strict derived quotient augmentation to the constant completion unit. For every finite list a generating the adic ideal and every complex C, the same F carries the localized intrinsic Koszul fiber of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] to constant quotient completion of F(Q(C)), carrying its specified fiber unit to the same completion unit. No completeness assumption on K or C is made.

source.place: current order 1316, Koszul-to-quotient comparison, including its unit equation

proof.text: Choose the scalar-preserving completed-ring and module equivalences and the normalized strict quotient-tower comparison.

Use the canonical native and constant localizations and their universal derived pairs. Take the induced equivalences on complexes and derived categories. The ordinary quotient-tower comparison and preservation of inverse limits induce compatible left- and right-derived comparison squares.

Choose a native K-flat representative of K. Normalize the actual quotient-completion unit and the constant quotient-completion unit as localized ordinary limit cones followed by their universal inverse-limit comparisons. Their ordinary cones agree because all finite projections agree.

Use the generic normalized-completion transport API, keeping all ordinary and derived functors abstract in its unit calculation. The right-derived comparison equation identifies the two normalized limit-cone maps. The left-derived comparison equation identifies their reduction counits. The actual reduction counit is invertible on the chosen K-flat complex; cancellation therefore identifies the completion units. Transport this comparison along the realization isomorphism to K.
The scalar-preserving Koszul comparison gives the second clause for the same derived equivalence, using its canonical localization factorization.

proof_origin.place: Formal comparison and unit-normalization details of the recorded Koszul/quotient reconstruction; proved from the existing universal and reflector interfaces.

mathlib_searches.verdict: No exact match for the sheaf coefficient presentation or its derived unit.
Useful universal comparison API, but no concrete completed-sheaf unit comparison.
